_comment_em_dash: rule-em-dash is disabled here because this marketplace's house style uses em dashes deliberately: measured 34,999 matching lines across 1229 tracked markdown files (2026-08-19), which is a style choice, not a defect backlog. Disabling beats enumerating em_dash_allowed_paths, which would need near-total path coverage to be useful. The shipped default stays zero-tolerance; this is the consuming repo's own decision, which is exactly what the config layer is for.
_comment_curly: rule-curly-artifacts is disabled here because punctuation glyphs were already ruled out of scope by the repo owner, twice in writing, and the rule's measured yield is almost entirely the material that ruling protects. Measured 2026-08-20 over 1214 tracked markdown files: 72 findings, of which 39 are quoted Pat Pattison book text, 32 are a verbatim pasted external Codex review, and exactly 1 was genuine paste residue (a stray curly apostrophe in plugins/disk-hygiene/README.md, fixed in the same commit as this entry). The rulings: plugins/songwriting/context/pat-pattison/research/book-references.md ('Do not sweep, measure, audit, or open work items on punctuation glyphs' — a session was spent on exactly that before the owner ruled it out of scope) and the songwriting CHANGELOG entry 'PUNCTUATION GLYPHS ARE NOT A FIDELITY AXIS — DO NOT SWEEP FOR THEM', which records a prior session normalizing 470 lines before the ruling. A per-path exemption would be the narrower instrument, but the config layer only supports that for rule-em-dash today; generalizing it is tracked separately. Revisit if a corpus of genuine LLM paste residue ever lands here: the shipped default stays on, and this is the consuming repo's decision, not the plugin's.
